A1.question: Does an absence conclusion require at least one supporting root, or is complete coverage alone sufficient?
A1.registeredTextImplies: coverage alone: an absence claim with complete coverage and an EMPTY evidence ledger concludes absent_within_declared_scope (conclusionFunction.absence has no support term)
A1.alternativeReading: absence requires >= 1 supporting root; the empty-ledger worlds conclude not_established
A1.consequence: The 4 affected worlds are the epistemically loudest receipts the schema can emit: bounded absence asserted with no evidence in the ledger at all (the independent implementer's F7/A1, maintained through all three of its runs).
A1.status: owner decision not reached; closed by text without a listed repair (G5); recorded, not decided

A2.question: Does a presence conclusion require complete search coverage?
A2.registeredTextImplies: no: conclusionFunction.presence has no coverage term, so 'supported' is reachable with zero searched locations
A2.alternativeReading: presence also requires search.complete; the affected worlds conclude not_established
A2.consequence: 19,152 of 110,840 receipt-producing worlds (17.3%) change conclusion between the readings -- the largest undecided surface in the kernel. A third implementation reading it the other way would diverge on all of them while passing every invariant (the G5/G4 combination). UNDECIDED: the program records this as an owner decision it did not reach, with both readings preserved. The independent implementer chose the no-coverage reading in IND-1 on the argument that presence is existential; the registered text agrees; neither constitutes a decision of record.
A2.status: owner decision not reached; recorded, not decided
